definitions.explanation: Describing something that lacks substance, meaning, or emotional fulfillment.
Describing efforts or actions that are meaningless or produce no results.

examples.japanese: {一人|ひとり}で{過|す}ごす{夜|よる}は{空|むな}しい。
{心|こころ}が{空|むな}しくなった。
{彼|かれ}がいなくなって、{部屋|へや}が{空|むな}しく{感|かん}じられる。
examples.english: Since he's gone, the room feels empty.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}が{報|むく}われず、{空|むな}しさを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: My efforts went unrewarded, and I felt a sense of futility.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}を{言|い}っても{空|むな}しい{抵抗|ていこう}だった。
examples.english: No matter what I said, it was futile resistance.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}らない{人|ひと}に{何|なに}を{言|い}っても{空|むな}しい。
examples.english: It's pointless to say anything to someone who doesn't keep promises.

notes:
FORMS:
・{空|むな}しい (dictionary/attributive)
・{空|むな}しさ (noun form: emptiness, futility)
・{空|むな}しく (adverbial: in vain, emptily)

KANJI VARIATIONS:
Can also be written as {虚|むな}しい, though {空|むな}しい is more common.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{空|むな}しく{終|お}わる - to end in vain
・{空|むな}しさを{感|かん}じる - to feel emptiness
・{空|むな}しい{努力|どりょく} - futile effort

SIMILAR WORDS:
・やるせない - forlorn, helpless (more about suppressed emotions)
・{物足|ものた}りない - unsatisfying, lacking (something is missing)
・{儚|はかな}い - fleeting, ephemeral

REGISTER:
Neutral to literary. Common in both casual and written contexts.
